-Establishing A Bike Boulevard, Requiring The Conversion Of Mountain Road And Silver To A Bike Boulevard, Requiring Design And Engineering, Providing An Appropriation To The Department Of Municipal Development In Fy/08 To Pay For The Design And Engineering Of A Bike Boulevard, Requiring An Update Of The City Of Albuquerque's Comprehensive Bike Facilities Plan.

+C/S Establishing a Bike Boulevard, Requiring The Conversion of Mountain Road and Silver To a Bike Boulevard, Requiring Design and Engineering, Providing An Appropriation To The Department of Municipal Development In FY/08 To Pay For The Design and Engineering of a Bike Boulevard, Requiring An Update of The City of Albuquerque's Comprehensive Bike Facilities Plan (Cadigan)

-WHEREAS, in seeking cycling paths, experienced cyclists seek fast direct routes while casual cyclists favor quieter streets whereas recreational cyclists prefer bike trials. For public agencies providing routes attractive to both groups can be challenging; and

-WHEREAS, Bike boulevards are a package of changes that transforms a residential street into a “bike expressway” which accommodates local motor traffic. The low vehicle volumes and infrequent stops attract all categories of cyclists; and

-WHEREAS, the low vehicle volumes enable cars to pass safely using the full street width, with no need for the separation provided by a bike lane stripe and also sweeping debris in the lane to the gutter.  Boulevards being ordinary streets with sidewalks have no dangerous path/street intersections or conflicts with pedestrians; and

-WHEREAS, converting a local street to a bike boulevard includes but is not limited to removing barriers and detours to through cycling, removing stop signs from the boulevard and stopping traffic approaching from intersecting streets, installing where necessary bike permeable street closures and mandatory turns that admit through bicycle, installing bike actuated signals at all crossing of the boulevard with major streets and appropriately signing the route; and

-WHEREAS, boulevards are less expensive then acquiring right-of-way for a side path or bike lane freeing funds for construction of grade separated bike crossing to bridge a bike boulevard over major barriers such as freeways; and

-WHEREAS, a bike boulevard on Mountain Road from Gabaldon Road to Woodward  Place parallels Lomas Boulevard and collects traffic from adjoining neighborhoods traveling to the Central Business District and the University of New Mexico; and

-WHEREAS, a bike boulevard on Silver Avenue from Park Avenue to Second Street parallels Central Avenue and collects traffic from adjoining neighborhoods traveling to the Central Business District; and
-WHEREAS both these routes will provide direct connections to the Bosque Bike Trail.

+ESTABLISHING THE CONVERSION OF LOCAL STREETS TO CREATE TWO  BIKE BOULEVARDS, PROVIDING AN APPROPRIATION TO THE DEPARTMENT OF MUNICIPAL DEVELOPMENT IN FY/08 TO PAY FOR THE DESIGN, ENGINEERING AND INITIAL IMPLEMENTATION OF A BIKE BOULEVARD, REQUIRING AN AMENDMENT TO  THE CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE'S COMPREHENSIVE BIKE FACILITIES PLAN TO INCLUDE BIKE BOULEVARDS, REQUESTING CONSULTATION WITH BIKE ADVOCACY ORGANIZATIONS.

+WHEREAS, when cycling, experienced cyclists seek fast direct routes,  casual cyclists favor quieter streets and recreational cyclists prefer bike trials. For public agencies providing routes attractive to all three groups can be challenging; and
+WHEREAS, Bike boulevards are a package of traffic tools that transform a residential street into a “bike expressway” that also accommodates local motor traffic.

+WHEREAS, a bike boulevard's low vehicle volumes and infrequent stops attract all categories of cyclists. The low vehicle volumes enable cars to pass safely using the full street width, with no need for the separation provided by a bike lane stripe.  Bike boulevards, being ordinary streets with sidewalks, do not have dangerous path/street intersections or conflicts with pedestrians; and

+WHEREAS, converting a local street to a bike boulevard includes but is not limited to removing barriers and detours to through cycling, removing stop signs from the boulevard and stopping traffic approaching from intersecting streets, installing where necessary bike permeable street closures and mandatory turns that admit through bicycle, installing bike actuated signals or mid block crossings at intersections with major streets and appropriately signing the route; and

+WHEREAS, boulevards are less expensive then acquiring right-of-way for a side path or bike lane freeing funds for construction of necessary amenities such as signage, mid-block crossings and traffic calming; and

+WHEREAS, a bike boulevard on Mountain Road from Gabaldon Road  to Old Town and through the Downtown Neighborhood Association Area to Tijeras Avenue and east to University Boulevard would parallel Lomas Boulevard, link to the Silver Avenue Bike Boulevard and collect traffic traveling to the Bosque Trail, downtown, the University of New Mexico, Central New Mexico College, the Hospital District and Nob Hill; and

+WHEREAS, a bike boulevard on Silver Avenue from Carlisle Boulevard to Cedar Street  and north to Martin Luther King Boulevard would parallel Central Avenue, connect with the Downtown Bike Boulevard and carry traffic to Nob Hill, the University of New Mexico, Central New Mexico College, the hospital district,  downtown, Old Town and the Bosque Trail.

-Section 2. That the Administration by  June 1st, 2008 shall communicate to the City Council for approval the design and preliminary engineering for converting the aforementioned streets to a bike boulevard.
-Section 3.  That the project scope for the Trails/Bikeways project activity
